Bobby Orr is a Canadian defenseman and arguably the greatest blue-liner in hockey history. His revolutionary skating ability and offensive contributions transformed how the position was played, winning two Stanley Cups with the Boston Bruins in the nineteen seventies.

He scored two hundred seventy goals and six hundred forty-five assists for nine hundred fifteen points as a defenseman, an unprecedented offensive total for the position. Orr won the Hart Trophy for MVP twice, the only defenseman to win it in the modern era before it became reserved for forwards. He led the Boston Bruins to Stanley Cups in nineteen seventy and nineteen seventy-two, including an iconic overtime goal in the nineteen seventy Finals that is often considered the most famous goal in hockey history.

He was famous for his explosive stride and skating ability, revolutionizing the defenseman role by joining the attack and carrying the puck into the offensive zone. Orr won the Norris Trophy for best defenseman for eight consecutive years from nineteen sixty-eight to nineteen seventy-five, a record unlikely to be surpassed. His career was cut short by serious knee injuries at age thirty, resulting in early retirement. Yet despite this, he remains one of sport's most influential figures. He wore number four and was a pioneer of the aggressive, attacking defenseman model that dominated hockey in the nineteen seventies.
